title: Users and agents resolve upstream Git conflicts

nodes.summary: Ordinary Git resolves upstream conflicts; Kyyn owns no remote adoption protocol
nodes.detail: Users and agents fetch, merge/rebase and push with ordinary Git and check the resulting KB themselves. Kyyn has no distributed coordinator, semantic merge or special conflict-resolution proposal; its acceptance guarantees only ADR 0012's conditional local step.

realised.evidence: Negative constraint; no code existed at founding and the host still contains no fetch/merge/push or remote-coordination code

nodes.summary: Acceptance publishes locally as Git history; no automatic force push
nodes.detail: Local acceptance is ordinary Git history advanced by a local conditional update; normal push may be rejected by an advanced remote and force push is never an automatic remedy. Local acceptance and remote publication are reported separately; a local CAS reserves nothing remotely.

realised.evidence: PR #23 adds expected-head CompareAndSwapRef; PR #42 composes acceptance as commit + local CAS; guide states acceptance 'does not push to a remote'

deliveries.evidence: PR #23 adds index-free commit construction and the local conditional branch update; composing acceptance from them follows in #42

nodes.summary: Unaccepted evolutions rebase in place; no permanent Stale lifecycle
nodes.detail: When head advances, the author sets Before.revision to the new head, refreshes schema, repairs and reruns the transformation in the same workspace, rather than creating a new workspace or keeping old attempts. Accepted workspaces stay as history.

realised.evidence: PR #42 tests 'acceptance/rebase/recovery journeys'; BaseMismatch reports expected vs actual head; guide says update Before and re-check; lifecycle is Draft/Ready/Accepted only

nodes.summary: Drafts stay local; no implicit session-sync service
nodes.detail: Uncommitted drafts live on one machine; sharing them requires ordinary Git commit/push or explicit file transfer. Kyyn provides no session synchronisation.

realised.evidence: Negative constraint; no sync service exists at any point

nodes.summary: Explicit repository and KB path; whole-repository CAS for shared repos
nodes.detail: Semantic operations take an explicit repository and KB path rather than ambient cwd. When several KBs share one repository, whole-repository CAS conservatively conflicts; no cross-KB transactions or branch-per-KB federation.

realised.evidence: Porcelain operations carry an explicit KnowledgeBase(Repository) value and acceptance CASes the repo branch head; PR #44 CLI adds --kb PATH with Git repo discovery (though --kb defaults to '.')

deliveries.evidence: PR #31 introduces explicit KnowledgeBase values (repository plus KB prefix) carried by porcelain operations; whole-repository CAS and CLI --kb selection were still missing
PR #42 acceptance CASes the repository branch head, so KBs sharing a repository conflict conservatively; CLI --kb with repository discovery follows in #44

editorial.note: Front-matter/status cleanup and dropping 'proposed' from the ADR 0012 cross-reference; no change in what the architecture requires

notes: A tiny, stable lane: founded once and only touched by the seq-143 metadata reconciliation. Most of it is negative constraints (no remote protocol, no sync service, no Stale state) which the code honours trivially - the host has no push/fetch code at all. The positive commitments (local CAS publication, rebase-in-place) were realised by the ADR 0012 acceptance work (PRs #23/#42) without ever editing this ADR. One soft spot: 'require an explicit repository and KB path; do not rely on ambient cwd' is met at the porcelain layer, but the CLI's --kb defaults to '.', so the surface does use cwd as a default.
